{"passages":[{"reference":"1.17","text":"And I set out my purpose from the beginning, how I had exhausted myself in insoluble inquiries, and everything that I disclosed to you at the outset, so that I may not write the same things again. I said, “I am quite ready to travel with you—for, though I do not know how, this is what I gladly desire. But first I want to be fully assured about the truth, so that I may know whether the soul proves to be mortal or is immortal; whether, if it is eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here; whether there is ever anything just or pleasing to God; whether the world came into being and why it came into being; whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved; and whether it will be better or will not even exist.” And, to avoid speaking item by item, I said that I wanted to learn these things and those that follow from them.

In reply he said, “I will briefly give you knowledge of the things that exist, Clement; for the present, hear from that knowledge.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς ζητήσεις ἀπόρους ἐκενώθην","chosen":"I had exhausted myself in insoluble inquiries","rationale":"The passive form of κενόω is figurative here: the inquiries had left the speaker spent or emptied, while ἄπορος describes questions offering no way through."},{"source_quote":"τοῦτο γὰρ οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως χαίρων θέλω","chosen":"for, though I do not know how, this is what I gladly desire","rationale":"The rendering preserves the parenthetical uncertainty of οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως and the positive force of χαίρων θέλω; alternatively, the phrase may mean “for somehow—I do not know how—I gladly desire this.”"},{"source_quote":"περὶ ἀληθείας πρῶτον πληροφορηθῆναι","chosen":"first I want to be fully assured about the truth","rationale":"πληροφορέω denotes being brought to full assurance or certainty, not merely receiving information."},{"source_quote":"περὶ ὧν ἔπραξεν ἐνταῦθα ἔχει κριθῆναι","chosen":"it is to be judged for what it has done here","rationale":"ἔχει with the infinitive expresses what is appointed or bound to occur; the feminine subject remains the soul."},{"source_quote":"εἴ τι ποτ᾿ ἔστιν δίκαιον ἢ ἀρέσκον θεῷ","chosen":"whether there is ever anything just or pleasing to God","rationale":"τι ποτε asks whether any such thing exists at all, while both adjectives remain coordinated."},{"source_quote":"καὶ εἰ κρείττων ἔσται ἢ οὐδὲ ἔσται","chosen":"and whether it will be better or will not even exist","rationale":"οὐδέ supplies emphatic negation: the alternative to the world being better is that it will not even exist, not merely that it will no longer exist."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾿ εἶδος λέγω","chosen":"to avoid speaking item by item","rationale":"κατ᾿ εἶδος can mean by individual form, category, or particular item; the context abbreviates a longer enumeration."},{"source_quote":"τὰ νῦν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἄκουσον","chosen":"for the present, hear from that knowledge","rationale":"τὰ νῦν is temporal, while αὐτῆς most naturally refers back to the promised knowledge; “hear the present points from it” is also possible."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.18","text":"God’s counsel has come to be hidden in many ways. First: bad initial instruction, evil upbringing, pernicious habit, bad company, and mistaken preconception. Because of these, error, then fearlessness, unbelief, sexual immorality, love of money, empty glory, and countless other such evils, like a mass of smoke occupying the world as a single house and clouding the vision of the men living inside, did not allow them, when they looked up, to discern from the design the God who made it or to recognize what pleases him.

Therefore, the lovers of truth who are inside must cry out from their breasts and summon help with truth-loving reasoning, so that someone who is outside the smoke-filled house may approach and open a door. Then the sunlight outside can be admitted into the house, and the smoke from the fire inside can be driven out.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ βουλὴ ἐν ἀδήλῳ γέγονεν","chosen":"God’s counsel has come to be hidden","rationale":"ἐν ἀδήλῳ describes something placed in obscurity or uncertainty; “has become obscure” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"εἰσαγωγὴ κακή, συντροφία πονηρά","chosen":"bad initial instruction, evil upbringing","rationale":"εἰσαγωγή is an introduction or initial course of instruction, while συντροφία can denote nurture or upbringing as well as companionship."},{"source_quote":"ἀφοβία","chosen":"fearlessness","rationale":"The term literally denotes absence of fear; in this catalogue it likely means culpable lack of fear, but the translation preserves the concise wording."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἕνα οἶκον οἰκοῦντα τὸν κόσμον","chosen":"occupying the world as a single house","rationale":"The participle continues the smoke image and presents the world as the one house filled by the mass of evils."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ τῆς διαγραφῆς","chosen":"from the design","rationale":"διαγραφή may denote an outline, depiction, plan, or ordered design; “design” fits the inference from the visible world to its maker."},{"source_quote":"ἐπικουρίαν προσκαλέσασθαι φιλαλήθει λογισμῷ","chosen":"summon help with truth-loving reasoning","rationale":"The dative φιλαλήθει λογισμῷ is taken instrumentally; it could also characterize the reasoning with which they cry out."},{"source_quote":"τὸ μὲν ἐκτὸς τοῦ ἡλίου φῶς","chosen":"the sunlight outside","rationale":"The phrase contrasts the light outside the house with the smoke inside; a more formal rendering is “the external light of the sun.”"},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ ἐντὸς τοῦ πυρὸς ὢν ἐκβληθῆναι καπνός","chosen":"the smoke from the fire inside can be driven out","rationale":"The word order permits either “the smoke from the fire inside” or “the smoke inside, arising from the fire”; the former keeps the spatial contrast clear."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.19","text":"By “the helper,” then, I mean the man who is the true prophet. He alone can illuminate human souls, so that we may be able to see with our own eyes the road of eternal salvation. Otherwise this is impossible, as you yourself know, having said a little earlier that every thesis can be refuted and established, and that the same thesis comes to be regarded as true and false according to the ability of the person defending it. Consequently, theses no longer appear as what they are but, depending on their defenders, acquire the appearance of being or not being true or false.

For this reason, the whole matter of piety needed a true prophet, so that he might tell us what exists as it is and how one must believe about everything. One must therefore first test the prophet by the full prophetic examination and recognize him as true. After that, one must believe him in everything and no longer scrutinize each individual thing said by him, but receive those things as certain. They are apparently received by faith, but in fact by secure judgment; for by a single proof from the outset and by a precise examination from every side, all things have been rightly grasped by sound reasoning. Therefore, above all else, one must seek the true prophet, because without him it is impossible for anything certain to be available to human beings.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸν μὲν οὖν βοηθὸν ἄνδρα τὸν ἀληθῆ προφήτην λέγω","chosen":"By “the helper,” then, I mean the man who is the true prophet","rationale":"The two accusative expressions stand in apposition: the assisting man is identified as the true prophet."},{"source_quote":"ὥστ’ ἂν αὐτοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς","chosen":"so that we may be able to see with our own eyes","rationale":"αὐτοῖς is intensive here, emphasizing direct sight rather than sight mediated by another person."},{"source_quote":"ὡς οἶσθα καὶ σύ, μικρῷ τάχιον εἰπὼν","chosen":"as you yourself know, having said a little earlier","rationale":"The nominative participle εἰπών is taken with the explicit local subject σύ, making the addressee the person who stated the point a little earlier."},{"source_quote":"πᾶσα ὑπόθεσις ἀνασκευάζεται καὶ κατασκευάζεται","chosen":"every thesis can be refuted and established","rationale":"In argumentative usage, ἀνασκευάζω means dismantle or refute a case, while κατασκευάζω means construct or establish it."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὴν τοῦ ἐκδικοῦντος δύναμιν","chosen":"according to the ability of the person defending it","rationale":"ἐκδικέω here concerns advocacy or defense of a position, not punishment or vengeance."},{"source_quote":"προφήτου ἀληθοῦς ὅλον τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας ἐδεήθη πρᾶγμα","chosen":"the whole matter of piety needed a true prophet","rationale":"The genitive προφήτου depends on the verb of need, and τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας πρᾶγμα denotes the entire undertaking or matter of piety."},{"source_quote":"πάσῃ τῇ προφητικῇ ἐξετάσει","chosen":"by the full prophetic examination","rationale":"The articular singular ἐξετάσει presents the prophetic examination as a whole, while πάσῃ gives it comprehensive force rather than dividing it into separate tests."},{"source_quote":"δοκούσῃ μὲν πίστει, ληφθέντα δὲ ἀσφαλεῖ κρίσει","chosen":"They are apparently received by faith, but in fact by secure judgment","rationale":"The contrast distinguishes the appearance of unexamined faith from the prior reliable judgment by which the prophet was authenticated."},{"source_quote":"ἀποδείξει γὰρ μιᾷ τῇ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς καὶ ἀκριβεῖ ἐξετάσει τῇ πανταχόθεν","chosen":"for by a single proof from the outset and by a precise examination from every side","rationale":"The two datives are read as coordinated: the single proof is characterized as being from the outset, and the precise examination as being from every side. Alternatively, καί may be explanatory, making the examination appositional to the proof, but the coordinated reading most directly preserves the construction."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ὅλα ὀρθῷ εἴληπται λογισμῷ","chosen":"all things have been rightly grasped by sound reasoning","rationale":"τὰ ὅλα denotes the totality of the matters in question, while ὀρθῷ λογισμῷ identifies the sound reasoning by which they have been grasped."},{"source_quote":"βέβαιόν τι προσεῖναι ἀνθρώποις","chosen":"anything certain to be available to human beings","rationale":"πρόσειμι means to be present or available; “for human beings to possess any certainty” conveys the same contextual force."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.20","text":"And likewise he set my mind at rest by explaining to me who he is and how he is found, and by actually enabling me to find him. Through the discourse about the prophet he showed the truth to my ears more plainly than things seen before the eyes, so that I was astonished and wondered how, when the things sought by everyone lie before them, no one perceives them.

However, after the discourse about the prophet had been written at his command, he arranged for the volume to be sent to you from Caesarea Stratonis, saying that he had a command from you each year to write down and send you the discourses and deeds. Nevertheless, on that single first day, while only just beginning to speak about the prophet of truth, he fully assured me about everything. Then he spoke as follows:

“From now on, observe the debates that I conduct against the opponents. Even if I come off worse, I am not afraid that you will doubt the truth handed down to you, since you know that it was I who appeared to be defeated, not the thesis handed down to us through the prophet. Still, I hope not to come off worse even in the testing debate, at least in the judgment of those who have understanding—I mean lovers of truth. They can recognize which arguments are persuasive, artfully constructed, and entertaining, and which are plain and simple, relying only on the truth conveyed through them.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς ἀνέπαυσέν με","chosen":"likewise he set my mind at rest","rationale":"The translation follows the supplied ὁμῶς as an adverb of similarity and takes ἀναπαύω figuratively as relieving uncertainty."},{"source_quote":"ἀληθῶς εὑρετόν μοι παρασχὼν αὐτόν","chosen":"by actually enabling me to find him","rationale":"Literally, the speaker was provided with the prophet as someone truly findable; the English expresses the resulting ability without adding an identity."},{"source_quote":"τῇ τοῦ προφήτου ὁμιλίᾳ","chosen":"through the discourse about the prophet","rationale":"The genitive is read objectively because the preceding explanation concerns who the prophet is. “Through the prophet’s discourse” remains grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"τῶν πᾶσι ζητουμένων ἔμπροσθεν κειμένων","chosen":"when the things sought by everyone lie before them","rationale":"The genitive absolute presents the sought realities as already lying openly before people."},{"source_quote":"τὸν τόμον","chosen":"the volume","rationale":"τόμος here denotes a written book-roll or volume containing the discourse."},{"source_quote":"τὰς καθ’ ἕκαστον ἐνιαυτὸν ὁμιλίας τε καὶ πράξεις γράφοντα διαπέμπειν σοι","chosen":"each year to write down and send you the discourses and deeds","rationale":"καθ’ ἕκαστον ἐνιαυτόν is taken adverbially with the recurring writing and dispatch; it could instead characterize the contents as “the discourses and deeds of each year.”"},{"source_quote":"Ἐνόρα τοῦ λοιποῦ","chosen":"From now on, observe","rationale":"ἐνοράω calls for attentive observation, while τοῦ λοιποῦ marks the time from this point onward."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς παραδοθείσης σοι ἀληθείας διακριθήσῃ","chosen":"you will doubt the truth handed down to you","rationale":"In this context διακρίνω denotes inward wavering or doubt, though “be divided in judgment about” is more formally possible."},{"source_quote":"εἰδὼς ὅτι ἐγὼ ἡττᾶσθαι ἔδοξα","chosen":"since you know that it was I who appeared to be defeated","rationale":"εἰδώς is attached to the explicitly addressed σύ because the point is that the hearer can distinguish the debater’s apparent defeat from that of the thesis. Attachment to the speaker, “since I know,” is also syntactically possible."},{"source_quote":"ἐν τῷ ἐξεταστικῷ λόγῳ","chosen":"in the testing debate","rationale":"ἐξεταστικός characterizes the λόγος as examining, testing, or critically probing the positions under debate; it does not describe an argument that is itself merely under examination."},{"source_quote":"πιθανοὶ ἔντεχνοί τε καὶ ἐπιτερπεῖς","chosen":"persuasive, artfully constructed, and entertaining","rationale":"The three adjectives describe rhetorical appeal, technical craftsmanship, and pleasurable effect, in contrast with plain arguments relying on truth alone."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς","issue":"The supplied, image-checked print has ὁμῶς, which can support “likewise,” whereas the much more usual concessive adverb ὅμως would mean “nevertheless.” The translation preserves the printed form; the interpretation remains provisional rather than silently adopting the conjecture.","proposed_reading":"ὅμως","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"πλὴν γράψας τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον","issue":"The nominative active participle γράψας would ordinarily share the subject of ἐποίησεν, but the genitive absolute αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος and the surrounding first-person narrative make the identities of the writer, commander, and person arranging dispatch uncertain. The translation uses an English passive for the writing event to avoid assigning an unsupported identity; a same-subject rendering, “after writing the discourse … he arranged,” is grammatically possible but leaves the command-giver’s referent unresolved.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
